sections.html:
The city of Spokane is both the seat and the largest city of Spokane County, in eastern Washington. About 558,344 people live across roughly 1,764 square miles, 241,434 housing units in all. Outside the city, residential areas include Nine Mile Falls, Newman Lake, Greenacres, Peone and Veradale.

A median owned home is valued at $410,700, and owners live in 64.5% of homes. Schools are split among many districts, including Spokane Public Schools, Central Valley, Mead, East Valley, West Valley, Cheney, Deer Park and Medical Lake, and your district affects the school levy on your bill. The Assessor appraises about 212,000 real property parcels.

The Assessor values property, the Treasurer sends bills and collects, and the Board of Equalization is an independent body that decides appeals. About 56 taxing districts send budgets to the Assessor each November, and the Assessor converts them into levy rates in January.

  • Treasurer: Spokane County Courthouse, 1116 W. Broadway Ave., Spokane, WA 99260; 509-477-4713; treasurer@spokanecounty.gov; open Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.
  • Assessor: 509-477-3698 for ownership, values and exemptions; 509-477-4787 for business personal property.
  • Payments by mail go to the Spokane County Treasurer, P.O. Box 199, Spokane, WA 99210.

The tax is payable in two halves, April 30 and October 31. A total under $50 is due in full April 30. A date landing on a weekend or county holiday slides to the next business day, so the next payment date to plan around is April 30, 2027 or the business day after it.

One statement a year goes out, with a coupon for each half. If yours has not come by March 31, call 509-477-4713 or find it on the SCOUT site, since a missing statement is no excuse for a late payment. Owners who pay through mortgage escrow still receive a full statement, and state law makes the taxpayer responsible for confirming the tax is paid.

Choices for paying include online by eCheck, debit or credit card, by phone, by mail and at the courthouse, where two drop boxes take checks only. In April and October the Treasurer also collects in person on set dates at Spokane Valley City Hall and the North Spokane Library. The online vendor charges 45 cents per eCheck and 2.65% on cards, with a $1.00 minimum. Mail is sorted by federal postmark under RCW 1.12.070, and a postage meter date does not count, so send it early.

First-half tax turns delinquent on May 1 and second-half tax on November 1. Interest is figured on the whole year's tax.

ChargeHomes with four or fewer units, and manufactured homesOther real property and personal property
Interest0.75% per month (9% a year) on current-year taxes1% per month (12% a year)
PenaltyNone3% on June 1 and 8% on December 1

Taxes billed before 2023 accrue at 1% per month. If the county mailed your statement to an address supplied by you or your agent, such as a closing agent, it cannot waive interest or penalty. A hardship waiver exists for a personal residence when the death of a spouse, parent or stepparent caused the missed payment, but you must tell the treasurer within 60 days of the due date and pay within that time (RCW 84.56.025).

To keep the right to sue for a refund, put a payment under protest in writing and include it with the payment (RCW 84.68.020). A returned bank item adds a $30 fee.

sections.h2: How the Assessor values a house
sections.html:
Every real property parcel is valued each year as of January 1 and physically inspected at least once every six years. New construction is appraised annually, and owners are told when a value changes. State law requires 100% of true and fair market value, based on comparable sales, depreciated replacement cost or income methods.

The Official Assessment Notice comes in June, but levy rates are not calculated until mid-January of the next year, so the notice cannot tell you the final tax. Individual bills are not capped at a 1% increase. That limit applies to some taxing district budgets, and special levies, banked capacity and annexations complicate it. When the market cools or stalls, assessed values follow, because they reflect sales information.

Appeal to the County Board of Equalization by July 1 of the assessment year or within 30 days of the date the Change of Value Notice was mailed, whichever is later. A mailed petition must be postmarked by midnight of the deadline, or you can hand-deliver it and have it date-stamped. Filing is free, and a letter or phone call does not replace the petition form.

  • The petition must give specific reasons the value is wrong, with the parcel number, the Assessor's value and your own estimate. Tax amount, other properties' values, the size of the increase and hardship cannot be considered.
  • Extra evidence must reach the board at least seven business days before the hearing.
  • You are notified of the hearing 15 business days ahead, and a written decision usually follows within about two weeks.
  • You may settle with the Assessor by a stipulation of value, or end the appeal by withdrawal.
  • You have 30 calendar days to appeal the board's decision to the State Board of Tax Appeals, or you can pay under protest and sue for a refund under chapter 84.68 RCW.

The Assessor is presumed correct, and you need clear, cogent and convincing evidence (RCW 84.40.0301). Keep paying while the case is open. One exception matters to buyers: the board can reconvene after the deadline if a new purchaser bought after July 1 and before December 31 of the assessment year at less than 90% of the assessed value.

The senior exemption is for owner-occupants age 62 or older with household income under $50,000. Apply through the Assessor's forms page or by calling 509-477-3698. Senate Bill 6162, signed after the 2026 session, sets new income thresholds for the senior and disabled persons exemption starting in 2027, so call the Assessor for the current limits.

The exemption also reaches people retired due to disability. A processed application produces a corrected statement from the Treasurer for you or your mortgage company. State law also requires every tax statement to describe the exemption and the deferral program (RCW 84.56.020).

If you pay off a mortgage during the year, contact the Treasurer to update billing information and request a duplicate bill. Failing to receive a bill does not cancel interest and penalty charges.

Get a written payoff for every unpaid year from the Treasurer before closing, and have the closing agent pay it from the proceeds. Interest accrues monthly, so the figure changes each month.

Mailed statements matter on closing day. If the Treasurer mails a bill to the address a closing agent provided and it goes unpaid, the county cannot waive the interest. Make sure your agent has the right parcel number and a forwarding address that works.

Real estate excise tax is due to the county treasurer on the date of sale, usually from the seller. The state portion is graduated. In the schedule for sales from January 1, 2027, the 1.28% bracket applies to the price between $551,000 and $1,551,000, and the local rate comes on top. Ask the Treasurer for the total.

If taxes stay unpaid for three years from delinquency, RCW 84.64.050 requires the treasurer to issue certificates of delinquency and begin foreclosure. Payments on past-due taxes must include the oldest delinquent year, with interest and penalties, before a certificate is filed or property is distrained (RCW 84.56.020). A cash buyer can close without a lender, and the title company can pay the Treasurer from your proceeds.

faqs.q: When are Spokane County property taxes due?
faqs.a: April 30 for the first half and October 31 for the second half. A bill under $50 is due in full April 30. The next date is April 30, 2027, or the next business day if that falls on a weekend.

faqs.q: What if I never received my Spokane County tax statement?
faqs.a: Call the Treasurer at 509-477-4713 or find the statement on the SCOUT site if it has not arrived by March 31. A missing bill does not cancel interest or penalty, because paying the tax is still your responsibility.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my Spokane County assessment?
faqs.a: Until July 1 of the assessment year or 30 days after the Change of Value Notice was mailed, whichever is later. File the free Board of Equalization petition form, and keep paying your tax while the appeal runs.

faqs.q: What interest does Spokane County charge on late tax?
faqs.a: A home with four or fewer units pays 0.75% a month with no penalty. Other property pays 1% a month plus a 3% penalty on June 1 and 8% on December 1. Interest is calculated on the full year's tax, starting May 1 for the first half.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Spokane County house that owes back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, if the unpaid tax, interest and penalties are paid at closing. Get a payoff from the Treasurer at 509-477-4713. Three years of delinquency lets the county begin foreclosure, so pay or sell before then.
